statement: Mira deposits $\$2{,}500$ in an account that earns $4.5\%$ interest compounded annually, and she makes no other deposits or withdrawals. After how many whole years will the balance first be greater than $\$4{,}000$?

choices.misconception: I set up 1.045^t = 1.6 but divided the base-10 log of 1.6, about 0.204, by the rate 0.045 instead of by log 1.045, which gave about 4.5, so I rounded up to 5.
I found that t is about 10.7 and rounded down to 10, but after 10 years the balance is only about 3,882 dollars.
I used simple interest, 112.50 dollars a year, so 1,500 dollars of interest would take 13.3 years, and I rounded up to 14.

hints: Solve $(1.045)^t > 1.6$ by taking a logarithm of both sides.
$t > \frac{\log 1.6}{\log 1.045} \approx 10.7$. Which whole number of years is the first that works?

solutions.reliable: We need $2{,}500(1.045)^t > 4{,}000$, so $(1.045)^t > 1.6$. Taking logarithms, $t > \frac{\log 1.6}{\log 1.045} \approx \frac{0.2041}{0.01912} \approx 10.68$. The first whole number of years that works is $11$. Check: $2{,}500(1.045)^{10} \approx 3{,}882$, which is too small, and $2{,}500(1.045)^{11} \approx 4{,}057$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
